transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I'm explaining this the right way. It's probably just stress, and I really don't want to waste your time, but I've been having a little trouble lately with... well, just these really awful doubts. 

Like I've missed something important. It could be a number on the mortgage payment, or a small clause in a client proof at work—I'm a graphic designer, so I really try to be careful with details, you know? Or even just a door not being latched at home. And the embarrassing part is, even when I know I checked it, the thought just barges right back in anyway. It just keeps telling me that this is the one mistake that's going to cost me everything. 

I know it sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud, and I'm probably making a bigger deal out of it than I should... but is that the kind of thing people usually come here for?
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking doors or rechecking your work, to try and get rid of these doubts?

Well, yes... I suppose I do. I mean, I'm sure everyone double-checks things to some extent, right? But I guess I might do it a bit more than I should. 

I... well, I end up reopening files I’ve already closed, or rereading emails just to be absolutely sure. And with things like bills, I’ll check the online payment confirmation... probably more times than necessary. Sometimes I even find myself saying the figures silently in my head, just over and over until they finally feel... settled, if that makes sense? 

I hope that doesn’t sound too strange. It’s actually a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, because it can turn a really simple invoice or just a minor logo revision into hours of extra time that I can't even bill for. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job and not letting anyone down, you know? Am I explaining that okay?
Do you feel like you have to perform these checking behaviors to stop the worrying thoughts?

Um, yes... exactly. I think you hit the nail on the head. Like I was just saying with reopening the files and rereading those emails... if I don't go back and do it, the worry just doesn't go away. 

I really feel like I *have* to check the payment confirmations again, or do that thing where I say the figures silently in my head, just to make the doubts quiet down. It's the only way to finally get that... that 'settled' feeling, you know? I really hope I don't sound completely ridiculous admitting this. It's just that if I don't do those things, I can't focus on anything else. And then, like I mentioned, a really simple invoice or a minor logo revision ends up taking hours that I can't even bill my clients for, which makes me feel terrible. 

Does that... does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel like these checking behaviors are necessary to prevent something bad from happening?

Well, yes, I suppose so... I mean, I don't really think the world is going to end or anything dramatic like that. I know it's probably fine. But... yes, I do feel like if I don't reopen those files or reread the emails, I might have made a terrible mistake that's going to ruin a client's project. 

And with the bills, if I don't check the online payment confirmations or... or do that silly thing where I say the figures silently in my head until they feel settled... I just get this overwhelming dread that I've messed up the family finances and we'll lose the house or something awful. 

I know it sounds so blown out of proportion when I say it like that. I really am a very capable person most of the time! It's just... I want to be absolutely sure I'm protecting everyone from my own carelessness, you know? That's why I end up spending hours on a simple invoice or a tiny logo revision that I can't even bill for. I just want to do things right. Is that... is that a normal way to feel about these things?
What happens if you try to stop yourself from doing these checking behaviors?

Well, I... I try not to let it get to that point, usually. I mean, I try to just do the checks quickly so I can move on. But if I'm in a rush and I actually force myself to close the laptop and walk away without... without doing the little routines... 

It's just really uncomfortable. I guess I start feeling this sort of buzzing in my chest, and I can't really concentrate on whatever I'm supposed to be doing next. Like, if I'm making dinner for my husband, I'll just be standing there at the stove, completely distracted, wondering if I sent the wrong file version. 

I usually end up just making an excuse to go back and check. Just once more, you know? Just to be safe. It's really not that bad, it only takes a minute to look again, and then I can be present with my family. That's the right thing to do, isn't it? Just taking a little extra care so I don't let anyone down?
Do these doubts and checking behaviors interfere with your daily life or relationships?

Well, I... I try really hard not to let it bother anyone else. My husband is incredibly patient with me, so at home it's mostly fine. But... um... I guess with my design work, it has been a little bit of a struggle lately. I hope it's okay that I'm sharing this. 

Like I mentioned before about the billing... because I'm taking that extra time to be absolutely sure, work that used to just take me a quick afternoon is now... well, it's dragging on for days sometimes. And because of that, I've had to push back a few deadlines, which I really hate doing. I've missed out on billable hours because I just can't in good conscience charge them for my own double-checking. 

And... this is actually really embarrassing to admit, but... one of my longtime clients actually reached out recently. They, um, they gently questioned whether I could still handle their simple revisions on time. I felt just awful. I pride myself on being a professional, you know? I'm just trying to give them perfect work so I don't let them down. 

I'm sure I can get it back under control if I just focus more and try a little harder. Does that... does that give you what you need to know? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checking behaviors in a specific way or order to feel settled?

Well, um... I guess so. I mean, it's not like a strict ritual or anything weird like that! I just... I have a little process, I suppose. 

Like I was saying before, when I'm working on a logo revision or sending off an invoice, I just... I like to reopen the files a few times, just to make sure the right version attached. And then I reread the emails. And with the billing, I always check the online payment confirmation, and... well, I do that thing where I say the figures silently in my head. 

I know I mentioned that already, I hope it's okay I'm repeating myself! It's just... I have to do it until it feels right. Until it feels settled in my mind. If I don't do it just like that, I can't quite shake the feeling that I've messed up. It's really just a way of being thorough, but... yes, I suppose doing it in that specific way is what ends up turning a simple task into something that takes hours. 

I'm really trying to get better about it, though. I know it's not the most efficient way to work. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How much distress do you feel when you're unable to perform your checking behaviors?

Well, um... distress is a strong word, I think. I wouldn't say I get distressed, exactly. It's more just... a little uncomfortable? 

Like I mentioned before, if I have to walk away without checking, I just get that sort of buzzing feeling in my chest, and I feel a little distracted. But it's really not unbearable or anything like that. I just try to breathe through it and focus on whatever else I'm doing, like cooking dinner or talking with my husband. 

I mean, I usually just end up doing the checks anyway because it's easier and it just takes a minute, so I don't really have to sit with that feeling for very long. It's really not a huge problem, I promise. I'm just trying to be careful and do things right. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough for you. I just wouldn't want you to think I'm falling apart over it or anything!
Do you ever feel the need to think specific thoughts or repeat certain words to yourself to relieve anxiety or worry?

Well, um... I guess I sort of do. I know I mentioned this just a moment ago, and I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, but... yes, with the billing and the files. 

When I'm checking the online payment confirmations or making sure the right logo revision is attached, I do... well, I do say the figures or the file names silently in my head. It's just a little habit! I just sort of repeat them to myself while I'm reopening the files or rereading the emails. I just keep doing it until it feels 'settled,' you know? Until I'm absolutely sure I haven't made a silly mistake. 

It's really just to be thorough, but... I suppose that is what ends up turning a simple invoice into something that takes hours that I can't even bill for. I'm really trying to stop doing it so much, though. I know it sounds a little silly when I say it out loud. Is that the kind of thing you meant? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right examples.
Have these doubts and checking behaviors affected your relationships with friends or caused you to avoid social situations?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, um... my friends are wonderful, and I definitely don't avoid seeing them! 

I suppose... well, sometimes I might be a tiny bit late to a lunch or a get-together if I get caught up checking a client file before I leave the house, but they just think I'm a busy designer. I certainly wouldn't say it's hurt my relationships at all. I try really hard to keep my little work habits separate from my personal life, so I'm always making sure to be there for people. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm isolating myself or being a bad friend, because I'm really not! I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay and giving you the kind of answers you need for this. Does that help?
Do you feel like you have to think about certain things in a specific way to relieve your anxiety?

Um... I'm not entirely sure I know what you mean by that one. I don't think I do? I mean, besides just repeating the file names and the billing numbers in my head like I mentioned a few minutes ago... I don't think I have to think about other things in a specific way. 

I really just try to stay positive and focus on my design work, or, you know, my family. I haven't noticed myself needing to think in a certain pattern or anything like that to feel less worried. 

I hope it's okay that I don't really have a good example for that! Am I understanding the question right? I just want to make sure I'm not missing anything you're looking for and that I'm being as helpful as I can be.
Do you feel like you have to think about certain things over and over in your head to relieve your anxiety?

Well, um, yes, I suppose I do. I know I keep bringing this up, and I really hope I'm not sounding like a broken record... but it's really just with the work things I mentioned before. 

Like when I'm checking the online payment confirmations, or making sure I've attached the absolute final logo revision, I do go over it in my head. I end up reopening the files, or rereading the emails, and saying the figures silently to myself. I just keep doing it, over and over, until it feels... settled, I guess. Until I'm absolutely positive it's correct. 

It's really just because I want to be a good designer and not make any silly mistakes, but... well, I know it turns a simple invoice into something that takes hours that I can't even bill for. I really am trying to get better about it, though! I know it's not the most efficient way to work. Is that the kind of thing you meant? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Would you say that your doubts and checking behaviors are causing you a lot of emotional pain or distress?

Oh, um... "emotional pain" sounds so... intense. I really don't think I'd call it pain or distress, honestly. I mean, I'm generally a very happy person! 

I suppose it can be a tiny bit frustrating sometimes, just because, well, I know I'm spending too much time double-checking those client files instead of maybe relaxing or getting ahead on my next project. But it's really just a little annoyance, you know? It's not like I'm sitting around crying about it or anything like that. I just want to do a good job for my clients, and sometimes my brain just wants to be extra, extra sure. 

I really don't want you to worry that I'm falling apart or terribly upset, because I'm definitely not! I'm doing just fine overall. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not downplaying it if you think it's a bigger deal, I just want to give you an honest picture of how I'm feeling.
